text:
maya: FYI I'm cleaning up the Dedicated autoscale/provisioning docs. Found ambiguous terms around eviction vs preemption and a misleading YAML example.

kevin: Link?

maya: current live page: https://docs.redwood.ai/dedicated/provisioning.html (section 'Eviction semantics'). The snippet uses `eviction: auto` which customers interpret as "we restart your containers automatically". That's not accurate for strict isolation or on-prem.

anna-sre: Correct. Behavior differs by pool config: 
- reserved (non-preemptible): nodes rarely die; runtime may reschedule transparently.
- preemptible: nodes can be reclaimed and workloads may be lost if no capacity.
- strict isolation (private): we don't perform automatic restarts in air-gapped setups; often manual ops required.

luca: Suggest replacing `eviction: auto` with an explicit `eviction_policy: drain | terminate` enum in docs to show the options and expected outcomes.

paul: Agree. Also add a short code example showing how to detect allocation changes via the SDK so apps can reconnect gracefully. Example idea: 
```python
# poll allocation state and backoff on reschedule
from redwood import DedicatedClient
c = DedicatedClient()
while True:
  alloc = c.get_allocation(aid)
  if alloc['status'] == 'rescheduled':
    # reestablish session
    reconnect()
  sleep(poll_backoff())
```

maya: I'll craft a PR that: 1) replaces the YAML with clearer fields, 2) adds a migration checklist for customers migrating from shared->strict pools, 3) includes the SDK snippet + guidance on session length and retries.

kevin: Add a short "expectations during scale" bullet list: scheduling delays, image pull time, and best practices for streaming calls (keep-alive, heartbeat).

anna-sre: Also add a small table showing expected availability delta for preemptible vs reserved nodes (we'll provide numbers). Note: SLA is product-level; don't promise different SLAs per pool.

maya: Good point. I'll include a footnote: "SLA applies to Dedicated product; pool choices affect operational availability."

luca: For the YAML examples, show a sample for `isolation: shared` and `isolation: strict` so customers can compare. Eg: 
```yaml
node_pool:
  isolation: strict
  preemptible: false
autoscale:
  policy: target_util
  target: 0.65
  eviction_policy: terminate  # terminates allocation on node preemption
```

paul: I'll add an examples repo PR demonstrating graceful reconnection patterns for websockets and batch jobs.

maya: Opening PR now to split the Eviction section and add migration.md with checklist. PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/docs/pull/1901

docs-bot: docs-ci: preview available for PR #1901 -> https://deploy.preview.redwood.ai/pr-1901/dedicated/provisioning.html (:eyes:)

kevin: Quick review: make the SDK snippet show exponential backoff and give suggested max session length when on preemptible pools.

maya: Will update. Also found one broken link to the SLA page, fixing to /dedicated/sla-matrix.md in the PR.

anna-sre: LGTM once numbers are filled in. Add a note for on-prem customers: manual reschedule may require support ticket if node images are pinned.

maya: Updated PR with backoff example and migration checklist placeholder. Marking WIP until SRE provides numbers.

kevin: Thanks — once SRE posts numbers we'll merge and publish with a short entry in #announcements and docs changelog.

maya: Yep. Planning a small post explaining the config change (eviction_policy) so infra teams can update their IaC. :rocket:
